domains.name: Introduction to SOC
domains.description: Fundamentals of Security Operations Centers: purpose, structure, roles, and operational models.
topics: What is a SOC? — mission, goals, and business value
SOC maturity models (Level 1–4)
SOC team roles: Tier 1 (Triage), Tier 2 (Investigator), Tier 3 (Hunter/Threat Intel)
Follow-the-sun vs 24/7 operations models
Key KPIs: MTTD, MTTR, false-positive rate, escalation accuracy
SOC tools ecosystem overview: SIEM, EDR, NDR, SOAR, TI platform
Communication protocols: shift handover, escalation paths, incident bridges

domains.name: Networking Fundamentals
domains.description: Core networking concepts every SOC analyst must know for traffic analysis and threat detection.
topics: OSI Model — Layer 1–7, encapsulation, PDUs
TCP/IP stack: IPv4/IPv6, TCP 3-way handshake, UDP, ICMP
Common ports and protocols: 22/SSH, 80/443/HTTP(S), 445/SMB, 3389/RDP, 389/LDAP, 53/DNS
Subnetting, CIDR, and network segmentation concepts
DNS resolution flow: recursive vs authoritative, DNS query types (A, AAAA, MX, TXT, CNAME)
HTTP/HTTPS: methods, headers, status codes, cookies, TLS handshake
DHCP, ARP, NAT, and common network services
Packet analysis basics: PCAP structure, Wireshark filters, tcpdump
NetFlow/IPFIX: flow records, conversation analysis, top-talkers
VPN technologies: IPsec, SSL/TLS VPN, WireGuard — traffic fingerprinting

domains.name: Cyber Threats & Attack Lifecycle
domains.description: Understanding threat actors, attack methodologies, and the Cyber Kill Chain / MITRE ATT&CK framework.
topics: Threat actor types: APT, cybercriminal, hacktivist, insider, script kiddie
Cyber Kill Chain: Recon → Weaponization → Delivery → Exploit → Installation → C2 → Actions on Objectives
MITRE ATT&CK framework: tactics, techniques, procedures (TTPs)
Unified Kill Chain vs MITRE ATT&CK — complementary models
Common malware types: trojan, worm, ransomware, rootkit, keylogger, RAT
Attack vectors: phishing, drive-by download, SQLi, XSS, brute force, zero-day
TTPs by threat actor: APT29 (Cozy Bear), FIN7, Conti, Lazarus, LockBit
Living-off-the-land binaries (LOLBins): PowerShell, WMI, certutil, mshta, regsvr32
Supply chain attacks: SolarWinds, Kaseya, 3CX — detection patterns
Ransomware playbook: encryption, exfiltration, double-extortion, leak sites

domains.name: SOC Tools & Platforms
domains.description: Hands-on knowledge of core SOC tools: SIEM, EDR, NDR, SOAR, Threat Intelligence Platforms.
topics: SIEM fundamentals: log ingestion, normalization, correlation rules, dashboards
Wazuh: architecture, agents, decoders, rules, alerts, FIM, SCA
Elastic Stack (ELK): Elasticsearch, Logstash, Kibana, Beats
Splunk: SPL search language, data models, lookups, alerts
EDR tools: CrowdStrike Falcon, SentinelOne, Microsoft Defender for Endpoint
EDR telemetry: process creation, network connections, registry changes, file events
NDR / IDS tools: Zeek (Bro), Suricata, Snort
Zeek logs: conn.log, dns.log, http.log, ssl.log, files.log
SOAR platforms: n8n, Splunk SOAR, Palo Alto XSOAR
Threat Intelligence Platforms: MISP, AlienVault OTX, ThreatConnect, OpenCTI

domains.name: Log Analysis & Correlation
domains.description: Reading, normalizing, and correlating logs across diverse data sources to detect suspicious activity.
topics: Sysmon — Event IDs: 1 (process), 3 (network), 7 (image load), 8 (CreateRemoteThread), 11 (file create), 13 (registry)
Linux logs: /var/log/auth.log, /var/log/syslog, journalctl, auditd
Web server logs: Apache/Nginx access logs, IIS logs, 400/500 patterns
Firewall logs: FortiGate, pfSense, iptables — allow/deny/reject patterns
DNS logs: query types, NXDOMAIN spikes, DGA detection, DNS tunneling
Email logs: SPF/DKIM/DMARC failures, attachment types, URL redirects
Cloud logs: AWS CloudTrail (S3, IAM, EC2), Azure AD sign-in logs, GCP audit logs
Log correlation techniques: time-window joining, session reconstruction, entity linking
Baseline vs anomaly: establishing normal, deviation scoring, statistical thresholds

domains.name: Incident Detection & Triage
domains.description: Detecting, validating, categorizing, and prioritizing security incidents in real time.
topics: Detection engineering: Sigma rules, KQL queries, Splunk searches, YARA rules
Alert triage process: receive → validate → enrich → classify → prioritize → escalate
First responder mindset: what to look for in the first 15 minutes
False-positive vs true-positive analysis: FP reduction techniques
Alert severity classification: critical/high/medium/low — based on impact and urgency
Triage checklists by alert type: phishing, malware, brute-force, data exfiltration
IOC extraction: IPs, domains, hashes, email addresses, registry keys
IOC enrichment flow: VirusTotal → AbuseIPDB → OTX → Shodan
Correlation with threat intel: mapping IOCs to known campaigns, threat actors
Case management: creating tickets, documenting evidence, timeline reconstruction

domains.name: Incident Response & Containment
domains.description: Structured incident response procedures: containment, eradication, recovery, and lessons learned.
topics: NIST SP 800-61 IR lifecycle: Preparation → Detection → Containment → Eradication → Recovery → Lessons Learned
Containment strategies: host isolation, network segmentation, account disablement
Short-term containment: blocking IPs at firewall, disabling compromised accounts, killing malicious processes
Long-term containment: patching vulnerabilities, rotating credentials, rebuilding systems
Eradication: malware removal, reimaging, vulnerability remediation
Recovery: restoring from backup, verifying system integrity, monitoring for re-infection
Playbook execution: ransomware, phishing, DDoS, data breach, insider threat
Evidence preservation: disk imaging, memory capture, log preservation, chain of custody
Post-incident activities: root cause analysis, lessons learned, report generation
Legal & regulatory notification: GDPR breach notification, CISO briefing, PR communication

domains.name: Threat Intelligence & CTI
domains.description: Collecting, analyzing, and operationalizing threat intelligence for proactive defense.
topics: Threat intelligence taxonomy: strategic, operational, tactical, technical (Diamond Model)
Intelligence lifecycle: Requirements → Collection → Processing → Analysis → Dissemination → Feedback
Indicators of Compromise (IOCs) vs Indicators of Attack (IOAs)
Structured threat intel formats: STIX 2.1, TAXII, MISP events, OpenIOC
OSINT collection: Shodan, Censys, VirusTotal, AlienVault OTX, GreyNoise
Dark web monitoring: TOR, I2P, paste sites, criminal forums, ransomware blogs
Threat actor profiling: attribution, TTP analysis, tooling signatures
Diamond Model: Adversary, Infrastructure, Capability, Victim
Operationalizing intel: creating detection rules, enriching alerts, prioritizing hunts
CTI reporting: daily threat briefs, weekly reports, campaign tracking, RFIs

domains.name: Vulnerability Management
domains.description: Vulnerability identification, prioritization, remediation tracking, and risk reduction.
topics: Vulnerability scanning: Nessus, Qualys, OpenVAS, Rapid7 — scanning methodologies
CVE/CVSS scoring: CVSS v3.1 vectors, base/temporal/environmental scores
Vulnerability prioritization: risk-based (EPSS, KEV), asset criticality, exploit maturity
Patch management lifecycle: assess → test → deploy → verify → document
Common vulnerabilities: Log4j (CVE-2021-44228), SMBGhost, EternalBlue, ProxyShell, BlueKeep
Virtual patching: WAF rules, IDS/IPS signatures, IAM policy hardening
Vulnerability reporting: remediation SLAs, exception handling, risk acceptance
Attack surface management: external asset discovery, shadow IT, cloud misconfigurations
Container security: image scanning, runtime security, Kubernetes CIS benchmarks
Cloud security posture management (CSPM): AWS Config, Azure Policy, GCP Asset Inventory

domains.name: Malware Analysis & Reverse Engineering
domains.description: Static and dynamic malware analysis, sandboxing, and identifying malicious behavior.
topics: Malware classification: trojan, worm, ransomware, spyware, adware, rootkit, bootkit, RAT
Static analysis: file type detection, hashing (MD5/SHA1/SHA256), strings, PE header analysis
Packer detection: UPX, Themida, VMProtect — unpacking techniques
Dynamic analysis: sandbox execution (Cuckoo, CAPE), process monitor, API call tracing
Memory analysis: Volatility — extracting processes, DLLs, network connections, injected code
Network indicators: C2 protocols, beacon intervals, DNS TXT exfiltration, HTTP C2 patterns
YARA rules — writing signatures for family classification and IOC matching
PowerShell analysis: deobfuscation, AMSI bypass detection, encoded command decoding
Macro analysis: VBA inspection, OLE extraction, Office exploit detection
Ransomware analysis: encryption algorithm identification, file extension mapping, decryptor feasibility

domains.name: Policies, Compliance & Governance
domains.description: Regulatory frameworks, compliance requirements, security policies, and audit readiness.
topics: Regulatory frameworks: GDPR, HIPAA, PCI DSS, SOX, ISO 27001, NIST CSF
GDPR: data subject rights, breach notification (72h), DPO, cross-border transfers (SCCs)
PCI DSS v4.0: 12 requirements, SAQ types, ASV scanning, network segmentation
ISO 27001: Annex A controls, ISMS, internal audit, certification process
NIST Cybersecurity Framework: Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover
SOC 2: Type I vs Type II, trust services criteria, auditor expectations
Security policy documentation: AUP, IAP, DRP, BCP, data classification policy
Compliance automation: continuous monitoring, evidence collection, reporting
Audit readiness: policy review, control testing, evidence gathering, remediation planning
Risk management: risk register, risk appetite, RMF, quantitative vs qualitative analysis

domains.name: Digital Forensics & Chain of Custody
domains.description: Forensic acquisition, preservation, analysis, and courtroom-ready evidence handling.
topics: Forensic principles: Locard's exchange principle, order of volatility (RFC 3227)
Live vs dead acquisition: methodology, tools, and when each is appropriate
Disk forensics: FTK Imager, dd, Guymager, EnCase, Sleuth Kit (Autopsy)
Memory forensics: Volatility 3 — profiles, plugins (pslist, netscan, malfind, dlllist)
Network forensics: PCAP analysis, NetWitness, Wireshark file carving
Registry forensics: SAM, SYSTEM, SOFTWARE hives — user activity, USB history, MRU
Browser forensics: Chrome/Firefox history, cache, cookies, bookmarks, downloads
Email forensics: header analysis, MSG/PST parsing, email threading
Mobile forensics: Cellebrite, Magnet AXIOM, iOS/Android acquisition
Chain of custody: documentation, hashing, tamper-evident logging, legal admissibility

domains.name: Advanced SOC: Threat Hunting & Purple Teaming
domains.description: Proactive threat hunting, adversary emulation, and purple team exercises to close detection gaps.
topics: Threat hunting methodology: hypothesis-driven, IOC-driven, TTP-driven (M-Trends, Sqrrl)
Pyramid of Pain: hash → IP → domain → host artifact → tool → TTPs
Adversary emulation: CALDERA, Atomic Red Team, Stratus Red Team, MITRE ATT&CK Evaluations
Purple teaming: bridging red and blue team objectives, joint exercises, metrics
Detection gap analysis: mapping attacks to existing alerts, false-negative identification
Sigma rule writing: YAML format, logsource, detection, condition, falsepositives
KQL/Splunk advanced queries: time-series analysis, baseline deviation, lookups, subsearches
Deception technology: honeypots, honeytokens, canary files, lures, breadcrumbs
Attack path mapping: identifying privilege escalation paths, AD attack surfaces
Automation & ML in SOC: anomaly detection, UEBA, NLP for threat intel, auto-response

domains.name: SOFT SKILLS
domains.description: Essential soft skills for effective SOC operations: communication, collaboration, and continuous learning.
topics: Technical writing: incident reports, executive summaries, playbook documentation
Communication: escalation calls, shift handovers, stakeholder briefings, war rooms
Time management: triage SLAs, multitasking, prioritization under pressure
Analytical thinking: root cause analysis, deductive reasoning, hypothesis generation
Team collaboration: working with red/purple teams, DevOps, IT engineering
Continuous learning: industry certifications (Security+, CySA+, GCIA, GCIH, CISSP)
Stress management: on-call rotation, burnout prevention, maintaining analytical accuracy
Mentorship: junior analyst development, knowledge sharing, internal training programs
